The proper way to use a cocktail shaker involves several steps. Follow these guidelines to ensure you create delicious cocktails:

1. Choose your tools: A classic two-piece cocktail shaker (also known as a Boston shaker) or a three-piece cocktail shaker (with a built-in strainer) will work well. You'll also need a jigger or measuring cup for precise measurements.

2. Prepare your ingredients: Gather all the necessary ingredients, including spirits, mixers, fresh juices, and garnishes. Make sure all ingredients are chilled before shaking.

3. Add ingredients: Fill the shaker with ice cubes, then add your desired amount of each ingredient according to the recipe. Typically, a cocktail should contain 1.5 to 2 ounces of liquor per serving.

4. Shake vigorously: Hold the shaker with both hands, ensuring the lid is securely fastened. Vigorously shake the cocktail for about 15-20 seconds, or until the shaker feels very cold and frosty. This process incorporates air into the drink, creating a smooth and creamy texture.

5. Strain the cocktail: If using a two-piece shaker, place a strainer over a glass and pour the cocktail through it. This ensures any ice chips or larger pieces of fruit don't end up in your drink. For a three-piece shaker, simply pour the cocktail directly into the glass.

6. Garnish and enjoy: Add a final touch by garnishing your cocktail with a slice of fruit, herb sprig, or edible flower. Serve immediately and enjoy your perfectly crafted cocktail!

Tips for making excellent cocktails:

- Use high-quality ingredients: Fresh, premium spirits, juices, and syrups will significantly impact the taste of your drinks.
- Measure accurately: Invest in a reliable jigger to ensure precise measurements of each ingredient.
- Chill your ingredients: Cold ingredients will help create a smoother, more refreshing cocktail.
- Shake thoroughly: Vigorous shaking helps incorporate air into the drink, resulting in a frothy, creamy texture.
- Strain carefully: Ensure your cocktail is free from ice chips and other solids before serving.

Results: More than half of the women (35/62; 56.5%) scored in the clinical range for FCR/P at baseline. Of the completers, 93% said that they would recommend the booklet to other women. "We are testing this to see 'how does this impact our brand, how does this impact our infrastructure, our own stores and e-commerce, do we reach new segments ... and of course also what will the result look like'," he said in an interview.

The trial marks another attempt to adapt to rapidly changing shopping patterns for the group, which until a decade ago almost solely relied on its giant out-of-town warehouse stores.
